name: The Odyssey — Odysseus returns home
summary: Ten years from Troy to Ithaca: lotus, giants, enchantresses and shipwreck stand between Odysseus and home. This is Homer’s legendary voyage, not a documented expedition. Dates are schematic and the disputed locations are illustrative map placements. Its knowledge events represent the poem’s circulation around 750 BCE, not Bronze Age discoveries.

stops.note: After the sack of Troy, Odysseus sails for Ithaca with twelve ships. The years on this route are schematic, placing the ten-year legend around 1200 BCE.
His men sack the city of the Cicones, then linger too long; a counterattack drives them back to sea (Book 9).
Wind and current sweep the fleet past the cape and away from home (Book 9).
Some men taste lotus and forget their wish to return. Plotted near Djerba as an illustrative placement; Homer gives no secure modern location (Book 9).
Odysseus blinds Polyphemus and escapes beneath his sheep, earning Poseidon’s anger. Plotted in eastern Sicily for this reconstruction (Book 9).
Aeolus gives him the winds tied in a bag. The floating island is placed among the Aeolian Islands for illustration (Book 10).
After nine days Ithaca is in sight, but the crew opens the bag while Odysseus sleeps and releases the winds (Book 10).
Blown back to Aeolus, Odysseus is refused further help (Book 10).
Giants destroy every ship except his own. This imaginary harbour is plotted near northern Sardinia; its location is uncertain (Book 10).
Circe turns his companions into swine, then restores them. They stay a year. Aeaea is plotted near Cape Circeo as an illustrative identification (Book 10).
At the misty land of the Cimmerians, he summons the dead and hears Tiresias. The setting lies beyond ordinary geography; the point near Cumae is only a map symbol (Book 11).
They bury Elpenor, and Circe warns them of the dangers ahead (Book 12).
The crew plugs its ears with wax; Odysseus hears the song bound to the mast. Plotted off the Sorrento peninsula for illustration (Book 12).
He sails between a devouring monster and a whirlpool, losing six men. The Strait of Messina is an illustrative identification (Book 12).

stops.place: Thrinacia — the cattle of the Sun
stops.note: His starving men kill Helios’s cattle. Zeus wrecks their ship; only Odysseus survives. Plotted by Sicily, without a certain identification (Book 12).
After drifting back past Charybdis, he reaches Calypso and stays seven years. Ogygia is plotted near Gozo only for illustration (Books 7, 12).
Freed by the gods, he builds a raft, survives Poseidon’s storm and is welcomed by Nausicaa and Alcinous. Scheria is plotted at Corfu for illustration (Books 5–8).
The Phaeacians carry him home asleep. Athena disguises him before he confronts the suitors and reunites with Penelope (Books 13–23).
